newsitem.title: USA: Albright urged to lift U.S. travel ban to Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Albright urged to lift U.S. travel ban to Lebanon.

text.p: A senior House Democrat on Thursday urged Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright to ease the U.S. ban on travel to Lebanon by American citizens that has been in effect since 1987.
Representative John Dingell of Michigan made the request in a letter to Albright a day after her Senate confirmation hearing.

"I, along with like-minded colleagues on Capitol Hill, believe that an immediate change of U.S. policy is not only overdue, but would help facilitate the more comprehensive settlement of the Arab-Israeli conflict you spoke of during your (Senate) testimony," Dingell said.

He said conditions in Lebanon have stabilised following the end of the country's civil war in 1990. Several Americans and other foreigners were held hostage during the war and many others were killed.
Dingell suggested the travel ban be replaced with a less restrictive travel advisory that would allow free movement of American citizens and commerce to and from Lebanon.
"I have been led to believe that the status of the travel ban is now under active review by the State Department, and any advice or assistance you could offer would be highly appreciated," he said.
Albright is expected to be confirmed by the Senate as the first U.S. female secretary of state shortly after President Bill Clinton is inaugurated for his second term on Jan. 20.
